postings.title: Business Development Executive
postings.description:
The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.



We’re looking for a Business Development Executive

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced outbound sales professional to join our direct sales team to qualify and convert leads in a fast paced and fun environment. You'll benefit from an uncapped commission structure, giving you full control over your earnings. OTE of £78k-£83k, with even higher earning potential available through promotion.



The role 

As a Business Development Executive you’ll build a high quality pipeline of prospects and generate revenue by making outbound calls, booking meetings, following up with customers, using Social Selling tools, and much more. Each interaction with a potential new customer is unique, and requires focus as well as solo thinking. How you manage your pipeline will make a significant difference in hitting your KPIs. If you are successful, the opportunity to grow and develop as a sales professional is unbounded.



Key responsibilities include:

 - Building and nurturing a high quality lead pipeline by making a high volume of outbound calls, and occasionally dealing with inbound queries, at all times representing the company in a highly professional manner

 - Using Social Selling tools & techniques to maximise your success in connecting with prospects

 - Identifying and qualifying prospects that might have a need for business finance

 - Communicating the iwoca value proposition in a precise and compelling way to engage and convert prospects

 - Going above and beyond in your efforts to hit and exceed your KPIs; this will enable us to beat sales growth targets

 - Working as a team player, and helping improve the overall success of this exciting part of the business.
   
   

The requirements

We look for people who are smart, humble, motivated and who are always looking to improve.

Ideally you'll:

 - Have past experience in sales, ideally within financial services

 - Be comfortable making cold outbound calls, and have an outstanding call manner

 - Be highly motivated, and excited to exceed targets

 - Be able to take on, and provide, quality feedback to power your own growth, as well as that of your teammates

 - Be organised and able to manage a large pipeline of prospects, with deals at various stages of progress

 - Be able to simplify and explain complex products in a way that customers with little experience in commercial financing can easily understand

Desired:

 - Understand the challenges facing small businesses

 - Have a good understanding of different financial products used by small businesses
   
   

Don’t take this list as prescriptive: it’s just to give you a sense of who might do well at the job. We’d still love to hear from you if you don’t hit every point on the list, or if you have other experience.



The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.



The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

 - Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

 - Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.



The benefits

 - Flexible working hours.

 - Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

 - A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

 - A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

 - 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

 - A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

 - Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

 - 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

 - An employee equity incentive scheme.

 - Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

 - Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

 - Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

 - A learning and development budget for everyone.

 - Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

 - Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

postings.title: Outbound Sales Manager - Deutschsprachig (m/w/d)
postings.description:
Wir suchen eine*n Outbound Sales Manager*in (m/w/d)

Wir suchen engagierte Outbound Sales Manager*innen (m/w/d), die unser neues Outbound Sales-Team mit aufbauen. Deine Mission ist es, kleinen und mittleren Unternehmen (KMU) zum Erfolg zu verhelfen. Du steuerst den kompletten Sales-Zyklus, von der ersten Kontaktaufnahme bis zum Abschluss. Dabei hast du als frühes Team-Mitglied die Chance, von Anfang an die Strukturen und Prozesse in einem Team mitzugestalten.




DAS UNTERNEHMEN

Gerade für kleine Unternehmen muss es oft schnell gehen. Chancen warten nicht und Liquiditätsengpässe können über Nacht entstehen. Um voranzukommen und zu wachsen, brauchen KMU Finanzierung, die genauso flexibel und reaktionsschnell ist wie sie selbst.


Genau deshalb haben wir iwoca gegründet. Unsere smarte Technologie, moderne Datenanalyse und unser erstklassiger Kundenservice sorgen dafür, dass Unternehmer*innen schnell, sicher und kontrolliert handeln können - genau in den Momenten, in denen es darauf ankommt.



Wir haben bereits mehr als 150.000 Unternehmen mit über 4,5 Milliarden Euro unterstützt. Unser Team setzt alles daran, noch mehr Mittelständler*innen zum Erfolg zu verhelfen - durch besseren Zugang zu Finanzierung und zusätzliche Services, die den Geschäftsalltag einfacher machen. Unsere Mission? Eine Million Unternehmen in ihren entscheidenden Momenten zu unterstützen und so einen nachhaltigen Beitrag zu leisten- sowohl für die Unternehmen selbst, als auch für ihr wirtschaftliches Ökosystem und die deutsche Gesamtwirtschaft.



Das Team

Unser Outbound Sales Team ist ein Grundpfeiler unserer Wachstumsstrategie in Deutschland. Da das Team gerade aufgebaut wird, erlebst du bei uns echten Gründungs-Spirit und hast die einzigartige Chance, die Prozesse und die Kultur entscheidend mitzuprägen. In einem schnellen und teamorientierten Umfeld ist es unser Ziel, deutsche KMU mit der Finanzierung zusammenzubringen, die sie für ihr Wachstum benötigen.



Die Stelle

In dieser Rolle hast du die Chance, als Gründungsmitglied eines neuen Teams dessen Erfolg von Anfang an mitzugestalten und genießt dabei Gestaltungsspielraum.



Die Anforderungen

Grundlegend:

 - Zeigt Neugier im Umgang mit KI-Tools und Interesse daran, diese weiter zu erlernen. Du nutzt KI bereits sicher in der Praxis, um Probleme zu lösen, effizienter zu arbeiten und die Qualität deiner Arbeit zu verbessern. Dabei zeigst du ein gutes Gespür dafür, wann der Einsatz sinnvoll ist, und kannst deine Entscheidungen nachvollziehbar begründen.



Dein Impact & Gestaltungsspielraum

 - Sales-Pipeline: Du baust eine hochwertige Pipeline mit potenziellen Kunden auf und übernimmst die volle Verantwortung für den gesamten Sales-Zyklus – vom Erstkontakt bis zum erfolgreichen Abschluss.

 - Analyse & Qualifizierung: Du identifizierst und qualifizierst potenzielle Neukunden und beurteilst, welche Unternehmen einen echten Finanzierungsbedarf haben.

 - Strategie & Teamwork: Du gestaltest die Vertriebsstrategie des Teams aktiv mit, indem du deine Erkenntnisse und Best Practices teilst, um unseren gemeinsamen Erfolg zu steigern.



Deine Entwicklung & Perspektiven

 - Expertise: Du wirst zum Experten für unser Wertversprechen (Value Proposition) und lernst, komplexe Finanzprodukte einfach und überzeugend zu erklären.

 - Weiterentwicklung: In einem unterstützenden Umfeld mit regelmäßigem Feedback entwickelst du deine Fähigkeiten im Pipeline-Management und im Sales stetig weiter.

 - Performance & Vergütung: Deine starke Leistung und das Übertreffen deiner KPIs treiben unser Wachstum direkt an und werden durch eine attraktive, ungedeckelte Provision belohnt.



Das wichtigste zu Dir:

Das bringst du mit

 - Du hast mindestens zwei Jahre Vertriebserfahrung und deine Ziele dabei regelmäßig erreicht oder sogar übertroffen.

 - Du bist sicher und erfahren in der telefonischen Kaltakquise und hast keine Scheu vor einem hohen Anrufvolumen.

 - Du bist sprachlich absolut sicher im Deutschen (C1) und bewegst dich auf Englisch verhandlungssicher.

 - Eine hohe Eigenmotivation und eine stark zielorientierte Arbeitsweise zeichnen dich aus.



Zusätzliche Pluspunkte

 - Du hast bereits Erfahrung im Vertrieb von Produkten oder Dienstleistungen an kleine und mittlere Unternehmen (KMU).

 - Du bist erfahren im Umgang mit CRM-Systemen (wir benutzen Hubspot) zur Steuerung deiner Sales Pipeline.

 - Du hast das Talent, auch komplexe Zusammenhänge einfach und verständlich zu erklären.

 - Mehr über die Vertriebsrolle erfahren Sie hier. https://www.iwoca.de/kredit/outbound-sales-manager-bei-iwoca
   
   

Du erfüllst nicht alle Punkte?

Sieh diese Liste nicht als strenge Checkliste an – sie soll dir lediglich eine Vorstellung davon geben, wer gut zu dieser Rolle passen könnte. Wir möchten dich auch dann unbedingt kennenlernen, wenn du nicht jeden Punkt erfüllst, aber andere wertvolle Erfahrungen mitbringst und davon überzeugt bist, dass du die richtige Person für den Job bist.



Das Gehalt

 - Wir rechnen mit einem Gehalt (OTE) zwischen 57.000 € – 65.000 € pro Jahr, bestehend aus einem Grundgehalt von 42.000 € – 50.000 € plus einem ungedeckelten Bonus. Uns ist es jedoch wichtig, dich fair zu bezahlen, also gib in deiner Bewerbung unbedingt deine Gehaltsvorstellungen an. Wir vergleichen Gehälter regelmäßig mit den marktüblichen Sätzen und führen zusätzlich vierteljährliche Performance- und Gehaltsreviews durch.

 - Um deinen Erfolg von Tag eins an zu sichern, erhältst du in den ersten drei Monaten 2/3 deiner Zielprovision.




DIE KULTUR

Bei iwoca gewinnt die beste Idee. Unsere Kultur basiert auf eigenständigem Denken, dem Hinterfragen von Annahmen und faktenbasierten Entscheidungen. Wir legen großen Wert auf Lernen und Weiterentwicklung und geben dir die Freiheit, dich in die Richtung zu entwickeln, in der du am wirkungsvollsten bist.

Wir sind ein Technologieunternehmen und glauben an das Potenzial von KI, uns schneller und besser arbeiten zu lassen. Wir schaffen die Voraussetzungen dafür, dass alle im Team jederzeit Zugriff auf die besten Modelle haben – und dass diese Modelle mit unseren Daten arbeiten können. Gleichzeitig unterstützen wir dich dabei, den Umgang mit neuen Tools zu lernen und dich mit ihnen weiterzuentwickeln.




DIE BÜROS

Wir geben uns viel Mühe, iwoca zu einem großartigen Arbeitsplatz zu machen:

 - Büros in Berlin, Frankfurt, London und Leeds mit reichlich Snacks und Getränken

 - Veranstaltungen und Clubs: Von Laufgruppen und Padel bis hin zu monatlichen Ping-Pong- und Billard-Turnieren




DIE BENEFITS

 - Ein smartes, motiviertes und internationales Team (wir vertreten über 35 verschiedene Nationalitäten) mit einem unbändigen Growth-Mindset

 - 26 Urlaubstage pro Jahr, plus ein freier Tag an deinem Geburtstag, die Möglichkeit, bis zu fünf Urlaubstage zu kaufen oder zu verkaufen, sowie unbegrenzter (unbezahlter) Urlaub

 - Ein 1-monatiges, voll bezahltes Sabbatical nach 4 Jahren bei iwoca

 - Direkter Zugang zur Unterstützung von zertifizierten Psycholog*innen mit unserem Partner OpenUp für Teammitglieder, die emotionale oder mentale Unterstützung brauchen

 - Zuschuss zur Fitnessstudio-Mitgliedschaft: 25 € für Fit711 oder den Urban Sports Club

 - 30 € Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket

 - Betriebliche Altersvorsorge über Canada Life

 - Top-Standorte: In Frankfurt direkt in der Innenstadt, in Berlin mitten im Prenzlauer Berg

 - Ein bezahlter Tag für Freiwilligenarbeit, an dem du eine gemeinnützige Organisation deiner Wahl unterstützen kannst

 - Voll ausgestattete Kühlschränke in unseren Büros mit allem, was das Herz begehrt: von gesunden Snacks bis hin zu Nervennahrung für den ganzen Tag

 - “Summer Houses” im Süden Europas und “Winter Houses” in den Alpen – bisher ging’s unter anderem nach Frankreich, Italien, Spanien und sogar noch weiter weg

 - Corporate Benefits Rabatte



Und damit das Lernen nie aufhört, bieten wir:

Hybrid in London or remote in the UK



We’re looking for a Data Scientist to join our Credit Risk Modelling team.

You'll work on the credit models that sit at the core of iwoca's lending business – the models that decide who we lend to, on what terms, and how far the product can grow.



The company

The team

The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and customer lifetime value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy.

The team is around twelve data scientists, who combined create models to efficiently drive fully automated and human-in-the-loop decision making. This forms the core analytical team that interface with and support smaller analytic functions in other parts of the business.



The role

As a Data Scientist in Credit Risk Modelling, you'll use iwoca's lending data to answer credit risk and CLtV questions, and build what you find into the team's production models. The work ranges from keeping today's models accurate as conditions change, through incremental improvements, to research that could replace them.

You'll help choose the team's projects and put forward your own. With AI, prototyping is cheap enough for you to test ideas that once wouldn't have made the priority list. The R&D share of the role is growing as a result. You'll learn credit modelling in depth from several senior data scientists.

Live examples of the work:

 - Causal estimation of offer terms. Estimating the causal effect of amount, duration, and price on customer outcomes.

 - Unifying automated and manual models. Finding a principled way to put the two model families, which optimise slightly different objectives, on a common cost function.

 - IFRS accounting model. Developing a multi-stage model where recovery predictions feed back to improve the upfront loss estimates that International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) require.

 - Generalising credit and CLtV. Exploring whether a single, more general model could replace the separate credit and CLtV models.



The requirements

Essential:

 - Applied statistics. You have a background in statistics from a quantitative field – typically a degree or Master's in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, or similar. You've applied it to real-world data, in research or at work. You know when the data breaks a method's assumptions, and what that does to your answer.

 - Probabilistic reasoning. You quantify the uncertainty in each estimate, and treat calibration as a first-order concern.

 - Research mindset. You've tested new modelling ideas of your own, and judged which were worth taking further.

 - Judgement. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right. You defend your reasoning under challenge, and challenge others' when the evidence points elsewhere.

 - Analytical ownership. You've taken ambiguous problems from framing the question to a decision the business acted on. You give an early answer and update it as new evidence comes in.

 - AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it – a prototype, an automation, or a modelling pipeline others use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't.

 - Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

 - Domain experience. You've worked in credit risk, lending, or customer lifetime value modelling.

 - Production ML. You've built supervised ML models end to end – exploration, training, deployment, and monitoring.

 - Non-linear methods. You can think in terms of the cost function and inductive biases of your models.

 - Bayesian methods. You've used hierarchical models, MCMC, or Bayesian updating in real work.

 - Time series modelling. You've modelled temporal data where autocorrelation, drift, or seasonality mattered.

 - Coding. You can write code for analysis. The team works in Python



The salary

We expect to pay from £60,000 – £90,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.



The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

 - Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

 - An employee equity incentive scheme.

 - Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

 - Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

 - A learning and development budget for everyone.

 - IFRS accounting model. Developing a multi-stage model where recovery predictions feed back to improve the upfront loss estimates that International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) require.

We’re looking for a Partnership Manager - manda (iwoca's M&A Platform)

We're looking for someone to build the introducer network that brings business owners to manda, iwoca's M&A platform. Accountants, solicitors, wealth managers and brokers meet an owner who is thinking about retiring long before we do. Your job is to make sure that when they do they think of us, and that referring us is the easiest thing they do that day.



The role 

Your mission is to build a referral channel that produces a steady flow of business owners who are genuinely ready to sell.



Today almost all of our sellers come from iwoca's own customer base, found by hand and worked one at a time. That works, but the pool is finite. The professionals who already advise business owners are the most credible route to the ones we'd otherwise never reach, and right now we have no systematic way of working with them.



You'll be starting from close to nothing, so the first version of this channel is yours to design. It also means the job is as much about making referrals actually arrive as it is about signing partners up.



It also has to scale. In this industry most partner flow still depends on people turning up at industry events, which works but stops the moment you stop showing up. We're after the version of this channel where referring a client to manda takes a couple of clicks inside the software an adviser already uses.



Key responsibilities include:

Build the introducer network

 - Find and win the firms worth working with: accountancy practices, corporate finance boutiques, solicitors, wealth managers and business transfer agents. Work out which kinds of firm actually refer, and concentrate there.

 - Do the outbound yourself. Identify the firm, get the meeting, make the case, and follow up until something happens.

 - Design what we offer them: how a referral is made, what the partner gets, what we commit to in return, and how we keep them informed once their client is with us.

Make referrals actually arrive

 - A signed partnership is worth nothing until a referral comes through. You'll own the ongoing relationship work that turns agreements into a flow: regular contact, keeping manda front of mind, briefing partner teams, and being the person they call.

 - Track referral volume and quality by partner, and be honest about which relationships aren't working so we can stop spending time on them.

Make the channel scale

Work iwoca's existing network

 - iwoca already has a broker network and a partnerships function with relationships across the SME economy. Working out where manda fits into those relationships is far faster than starting cold, and it's the first place to look.

Events and community

 - Build a focused programme of events worth attending and, where it makes sense, running our own: succession and exit planning, accountancy and adviser events, industry gatherings, and business owner peer communities.

 - Judge them on referrals rather than attendance, and stop going to the ones that don't produce. Events are how you find and land partners, not how the channel scales.

Prove the channel pays

 - Establish what a referral actually costs us once your time, any partner incentives and events are counted, and how many convert into a signed mandate. We have an assumption in our financial model and nobody has yet tested it.



The requirements

Essential:

 - Around 4+ years in partnerships, channel or business development, ideally B2B, where you built or substantially grew a referral channel rather than inheriting one that already worked.

 - You've done the full cycle yourself: identified the target firms, got the meetings, agreed the terms, and then managed the relationship afterwards.

Bonus:

 - Comfortable treating a CRM as a discipline rather than an afterthought, ideally HubSpot.

You'll build services that record each one exactly once, with no single point of failure, safe timeouts and retries, and graceful degradation when a dependency is down. When something breaks in production, you'll fix it so it doesn't break again.

You’ll learn iwoca’s financial products in depth, so you can challenge requirements and explain technical trade-offs to Finance.  - New ledgers. Building the ledgers for Flexi-Loan and iwocaPay.

 - Account migration. Moving existing loan accounts onto the new ledgers with zero downtime and no data lost.

 - Credit card ledger. Building new features for the credit card ledger, from real-time card holds to daily interest and monthly statements.

 - Reconciliation and journals. Reconciling the ledger with banks, payment providers, and the card scheme, and producing the accounting journals Finance relies on.

 - Funding facilities. Recording how loans move between iwoca’s funding facilities.



The requirements

Essential:

 - High volume. You’ve worked at a company where the volume of data or transactions shaped how you designed systems.

 - Migrations. You’ve moved live systems and data onto a new platform with zero downtime.

 - Python. You’ve used Python in production, with a web framework such as Django, FastAPI, or Flask. It’s the language the team works in.

 - Data tooling. You’ve built pipelines with Snowflake and dbt, or similar, that turn ledger data into reports for Finance.

The team is small – a principal engineer who leads it, another staff engineer, another engineer, and you. It works closely with the product teams that build on its ledgers, and with Finance.

You'll lead projects from design to production, and decide with product what the team builds and how. Every payment a small business makes with iwoca crosses several services and network hops before it reaches the ledger, and any of them can fail. You'll build services that record each one exactly once, with no single point of failure, safe timeouts and retries, and graceful degradation when a dependency is down. When something breaks in production, you'll fix it so it doesn't break again.

 - New ledgers. Building the ledgers for Flexi-Loan and iwocaPay.
